parts.note: reads as tourists at the spa city of Bath, but means people who visit a bath, that is, go into the water and swim

explanation.walkthrough: Bath is a Somerset spa city famous for its Roman baths, so 'Bath visitors' suggests tourists; the capital is a red herring for anyone in a swimming bath.
explanation.definitionFit: People who use a swimming bath are those who swim there.

clue.text: It's pleasant to be moderately successful

definitions.meaning: split into two words, to triumph in a few cases

explanation.walkthrough: Split as WIN SOME it means to succeed now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Charming and engaging describes someone pleasant, and winning a few is modest success.

definitions.meaning: a shift is a simple dress or chemise, which a seamstress makes

explanation.walkthrough: Split as MAKES SHIFT it is what a seamstress does when she sews a shift, an old word for a chemise or plain dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopgap device is a temporary expedient, and a dressmaker sews a plain shift dress.

clue.text: Are set in order for 'the Festival

indicators.note: put in order means arranged afresh, so the letters of those two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Preparations are made for a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In order' sounds like tidying up, but it tells you to rearrange the letters of ARE SET.
explanation.definitionFit: The spring Christian feast celebrating the Resurrection is a major church holiday.

parts.note: a cavalry unit led by its officer at the front, though the title belongs to an air force rank

explanation.walkthrough: A squadron is also a cavalry unit, so its leaders would head a charge; the title is in fact a Royal Air Force rank.
explanation.definitionFit: This rank commands an air force squadron, and the men at the front of a mounted squadron lead it.

clue.text: Prodigal gets a stroke of the whip about six

indicators.note: about means around, so the stroke of the whip is wrapped round the number

parts.note: a lash is a single blow with a whip
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A wastrel is flogged several times over.
explanation.definitionFit: A prodigal spends extravagantly, and lavish means given freely and wastefully.

parts.note: a nickname for a female pilot, a woman who flies like a winged creature

explanation.walkthrough: Split as LADY BIRD it suits a woman flier; it is also the spotted beetle.
explanation.definitionFit: A female flier could be called a lady who flies like a bird, and the name is also a red spotted beetle.

parts.note: the huntress is Diana, Roman goddess of hunting; her dinner, once eaten, is inside her

explanation.surface: A question about the condition of a hunter's meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as IN DIANA: the goddess Diana's dinner, once eaten, is in her.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is one of the United States.

clue.text: One sees them going right up the Strand !.

definitions.text: One sees them going right up the Strand !

parts.words: One sees them going right up the Strand
parts.note: the Strand is a London street, but a strand is also a beach, which the sea climbs at its fullest flow

explanation.walkthrough: The Strand is a main street in central London; with a small s a strand is a shore, and the sea at its highest reaches all the way up it.
explanation.definitionFit: At their fullest the ocean's flows reach furthest up the beach.

clue.text: Dangers for those mounting ladders on board

definitions.text: Dangers for those mounting ladders on board

parts.words: Dangers for those mounting ladders on board
parts.note: the board is a games board where climbing ladders is the aim and landing on the wrong square sends a counter sliding down

explanation.walkthrough: In the board game Snakes and Ladders, ladders carry a counter up and the other pieces send it back down; 'on board' sounds like a ship or a building site.
explanation.definitionFit: In that children's board game the serpents are the hazards that undo a player's climb.

parts.note: read literally, a dog lower down than another; in fact the term means anyone expected to lose a contest

explanation.walkthrough: Split as UNDER DOG it describes a low cur, but the phrase means the competitor given little chance, who need be neither canine nor contemptible.
explanation.definitionFit: The expression names the contestant thought least likely to win, whatever creature it is.

clue.text: A bit of a pig for drink

definitions.meaning: the head of a hog is one part of a pig
a large cask or measure of wine or beer, about fifty gallons

explanation.walkthrough: Split as HOG'S HEAD it is part of a pig; whole, it is a large barrel, so a quantity of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A big barrel of ale or wine holds a great deal to drink, and a swine's head is part of the animal.

parts.note: the 1 refers to the answer at 1 across, people in a bath, so the stroke is a swimming style rather than a golf shot or caress

explanation.walkthrough: The 1 points to 1 across, the bathers; the swimming style named after the chest suits them.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the standard swimming styles is named after the chest.

clue.text: Looking back, she was not well

indicators.note: looking back tells us to read the letters for being ill from right to left

parts.note: ailed means was ill

explanation.surface: A woman reflects that she used to be ill.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name stands for any female, as 'she' does in crosswords.

parts.note: a buffet is also a place serving food, and this one is in motion on a train

explanation.walkthrough: A buffet is a refreshment counter, and 'running' means moving along the rails.
explanation.definitionFit: The carriage on a train where meals are served is a buffet that keeps moving.

clue.text: A visitor would not leave it on Royalty

definitions.text: A visitor would not leave it on Royalty

parts.words: A visitor would not leave it on Royalty
parts.note: a caller once left a visiting card at a house; this one is a playing card showing a royal figure, which no caller hands to the king

explanation.walkthrough: Callers used to leave a visiting card; the king, queen and jack of a pack are pictures of royalty, so this card is not left on them but is them.
explanation.definitionFit: The king, queen and knave of a pack show royal figures from the court.

clue.text: Real chaos in a mixed choir here in Belgium

indicators.note: in places the first jumbled word inside the second
mixed means jumbled, so the letters of the choir are stirred up
chaos means disorder, so the letters of the first word are thrown about

explanation.surface: A Belgian choir of men and women descends into disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagram signals work here: 'chaos' scrambles the first word, 'a mixed' the choir, and 'in' nests the first jumble inside the second; Charleroi is a Belgian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Charleroi is an industrial city in southern Belgium.

parts.note: suggests figures from Thomas Hardy's novels, but means tough, enduring people

explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Hardy, the English novelist, invites a literary guess; the ancient Spartans were famed for endurance and austerity.
explanation.definitionFit: People of ancient Sparta were renowned for toughness, and the word now means anyone austere and tough.

clue.text: Where one might feel " on tov of the world "?

definitions.text: Where one might feel " on tov of the world

parts.words: Where one might feel " on tov of the world
parts.note: the idiom for elation is taken literally: the place at the very top of the globe

explanation.walkthrough: 'On top of the world' means delighted, but the cryptic reading is a place at the summit of the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: The point at the planet's northern end of its axis is literally at its top on the usual map.

definitions.meaning: Sir Stamford ... founded modern Singapore, whose famous hotel bears his name
A. J. ... is the gentleman safe-breaker in E. W. Hornung's stories, 'The Amateur Cracksman'

explanation.walkthrough: A cracksman is a burglar; Hornung's Raffles is a gentleman cricketer who steals for sport.
explanation.definitionFit: The founder of colonial Singapore shares a surname with Hornung's fictional gentleman burglar.

clue.text: A Lincolnshire borough has its advantages

parts.note: the clue words point to a town in Lincolnshire whose name is this word followed by 'borough'

explanation.surface: A market town in eastern England is well blessed.
explanation.walkthrough: Gainsborough is a town in Lincolnshire, an English county; its name is the answer plus 'borough', so the town 'has' the answer in its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Gains are benefits or profits, things to one's advantage.

clue.text: Can a rat change colour? Yes, to orange

indicators.note: to change is to alter, so the letters of those three words are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Can a rodent alter its hue? Yes, to a fiery shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change colour' reads as the rat turning orange, but 'change' rearranges CAN A RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Nacarat is a bright orange-red shade.

parts.note: a prize cup for the best layer, which would be the vessel that holds a boiled egg

explanation.walkthrough: A trophy is often a cup; the cup a hen would earn is the one her egg sits in at breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: A small holder for a boiled egg is a cup a laying hen's product earns.

definitions.meaning: read with the 'Not', having no fright at all

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a colloquial refusal ('Certainly not!'), and literally says someone has no dread.

parts.note: angelic means like an angel, beyond merely belonging to heaven

explanation.walkthrough: The A comes first in the clue but last in the answer; the charade needs no order signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Angelica is an aromatic herb whose candied stems decorate cakes.

parts.note: BA stands for Bachelor of Arts; its first part, bachelor, describes an unmarried man

explanation.walkthrough: The first part of 'Bachelor of Arts' is 'bachelor', and someone qualified as a bachelor is unmarried, perhaps sworn off marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living unmarried and abstaining from sex qualifies as a bachelor.

clue.text: Would a " No':Smoking"" order put some of them out of work?

definitions.text: Would a " No':Smoking"" order put some of them out of work?

parts.words: Would a " No':Smoking"" order put some of them out of work
parts.note: the people who prepare tobacco leaf, or smoke fish and bacon, would lose their trade if smoking were banned

explanation.walkthrough: Tobacco is cured, and so are kippers and bacon by smoking, so a ban on smoking would idle some of those who preserve them.
explanation.definitionFit: People who preserve tobacco, fish or meat by smoking or drying are the trade in question.

definitions.meaning: marsh plants with hollow stems used for matting
read as a verb clue: goes hurriedly, dashes

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the verb 'goes hurriedly', with 'hurriedly' standing for the whole idea of dashing.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterside plants used for thatch share the spelling of a verb meaning dashes about.

clue.text: They have every reason to be fallacious

definitions.text: They have every reason to be fallacious

parts.words: They have every reason to be fallacious
parts.note: the phrase 'every reason' is taken as clever reasoning used to argue for false conclusions

explanation.walkthrough: 'Have every reason' usually means have good cause, but here it means people who produce plausible arguments for falsehoods.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Greek teachers of rhetoric became a byword for specious argument meant to deceive.
